Class DeltaNetStatePool

java.lang.Object
smile.llm.model.qwen.DeltaNetStatePool
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public class DeltaNetStatePool extends Object implements AutoCloseable
Per-request DeltaNet recurrent and causal-conv state for linear-attention layers.

Recurrent state is typically float32 (fused CUDA kernel / stable in-place updates). Conv left-context must match the compute dtype (bf16/fp16) so decode concat(convState, hidden) does not promote activations to float and break later bf16 linear layers.

Multi-request continuous batching assigns each requestId a stable home row. activateStep(int...) packs those rows into [0, B) for the mixer; scatterActive() writes them back after the forward.

    • activateStep

      public void activateStep(int... requestIds)
      Packs bound request rows into working slots [0, B) for a forward.

      Working slots are the same storage as the first B home rows, so packing has to be careful in two ways. First, all sources are read before any is written (a sequential home-to-slot copy corrupts the cohort itself when homes are not in ascending order, e.g. once freed rows have been reused by later requests). Second, any live request outside the cohort whose home row lies in [0, B) is stashed and put back by scatterActive(), so a forward over one cohort never disturbs another's state (a speculating group and a plain-decode group alternate within one engine tick, for example). When the cohort already occupies rows 0..B-1 in order nothing is copied.

      Parameters:
      requestIds - bound request ids (order = batch).

    • ensureSpeculativeCheckpoints

      public boolean ensureSpeculativeCheckpoints(int numSlots)
      Ensures numSlots mid-verify checkpoint buffers sized for the currently activated batch (boundBatch), not the full pool maxBatchSize. Full-pool sizing OOMs under serving configs.

      Growth-only: never reallocates smaller for a later, smaller boundBatch (the early-return below already guarantees this), since a shrink would be pointless — the real reason growth matters is that any verify CUDA graph already captured against the old, smaller buffers becomes invalid the moment this reallocates (replay would then write into freed memory) — see the true-return contract below.

      Parameters:
      numSlots - checkpoint slots (N+1 for N draft tokens).
      Returns:
      true if this call reallocated (the caller must then invalidate any captured verify CUDA graph via QwenModel.invalidateVerifyCudaGraphs() before it can be replayed again).

    • ensureSpeculativeCheckpointRange

      public boolean ensureSpeculativeCheckpointRange(int firstSlot, int lastSlot)
      Allocates checkpoint slots firstSlot..lastSlot (inclusive) only, for max(1, boundBatch) rows. Slot numbers keep their meaning ("state after window position slot-1", slot 0 = pre-window), but slots outside the range have no storage: a save to one is a no-op and a restore from one is an error. In checkpoint-replay mode only slots 1..n are ever restored from (slot 0 is never read, and the last slot equals the working state), so allocating just those cuts the memory by 2/(n+2).
      Parameters:
      firstSlot - first slot to store.
      lastSlot - last slot to store.
      Returns:
      true if this call reallocated (see ensureSpeculativeCheckpoints(int)).

    • saveCheckpointForLayer

      public void saveCheckpointForLayer(int slot, int layerId)
      Copies active working rows [0, boundBatch) for a single linear-attention layer into checkpoint slot.

      Used by the verify-window per-position loop: QwenModel's layer stack is depth-sequential, so each layer's own forward (including its internal per-position loop) finishes before the next layer starts. A whole-pool save mid-loop would capture sibling layers' stale state; this saves only the layer that just finished its own position t.

      Parameters:
      slot - checkpoint index (0 .. numSlots-1).
      layerId - ordinal among linear-attention layers.
